text:
anya: noticed a weird artifact on the rollout PCTL chart: p99 lower than p50 for /v1/generate (eu-west) on canary slice :alarm_clock:
kevin: can you paste the slice values?
anya: canary-0.1 -> p50=130ms, p95=132ms, p99=98ms (from the console chart)
morgan: ok that's impossible for a single distribution: likely two origins merged with different scales or bad unit metadata
priya: quick check: backend_samples tagged unit=s, transport_samples unit=ms. backend values were like 0.098 -> got interpreted as 98 during rollup
kevin: that explains inversion. tdigest merge with mixed-scale samples can produce non-monotonic quantiles when weights differ
anya: product for canaries is confusing product folks. we should add a small provenance pill on the pctl legend that lists contributing origins and units
morgan: dev fix: normalize latency units at ingest (seconds -> ms) and tag normalized=true. fallback: block merge when unit tag conflicts and mark series as "mixed_units"
priya: UX: show a red tooltip on the chart when pctl provenance != single_origin saying "Mixed sample origins detected: values may be incomparable"
metrics-bot: scan-run: in last 48h found 5 charts with p99 < p50; first hit endpoint=/v1/generate slice=canary-0.1 region=eu-west
kevin: i'll open an ingestion patch to coerce latency to ms and add unit_inferred metadata for legacy sources (target: PR by EOD)
anya: i'll update the canary incident note and add a small blurb in the rollout docs explaining provenance badges
morgan: follow-up: add an alert rule when p99 < p50 for any slice so we can catch regressions automatically
priya: thanks all. small change but big UX impact. :+1:
